name: Phase 10: capture-driven fixture regression tests
checks: npm run check passed: typecheck, build, 525 passed / 0 failed (was 520), docs:check 17 files, validate 31 build files; plus a mutation check that the new suite fails when a section alias is removed
result: Phase 10 of the multiple-LinkedIn-UI support guide: fixture-based regression tests, and linkedom declined with reasons. THE DEPENDENCY DECISION: the guide offers linkedom 'if approved' and it was declined for three disqualifying reasons, recorded in the new suite's own header. linkedom has no layout, so innerText collapses to textContent - and every parser here consumes toLines(element.innerText), so a fixture would have to be crafted such that textContent happened to produce the right newlines, which is testing a fiction. No layout means no isVisible, which gates every heading, control, block and candidate panel - so either nothing is visible and the readers return nothing, or it is stubbed, at which point the program under test is not the program that ships. And there is no scrollHeight/clientHeight/getBoundingClientRect, so the scroll chooser and the reveal walk stay untestable regardless. A green suite that misrepresents live behaviour is worse than no suite. WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD: a fixture is the Phase 9 capture's DOM-free projection - per section, the exact line arrays the readers consumed, plus the heading list with the key each one resolved to - replayed through the real pure parsers with zero dependencies. That is precisely the half a linkedom fixture could not test faithfully. Two fixtures, both generated by running the real buildApplicantCapture, so neither contains an address, a number or anybody's name. PROVENANCE IS IN THE FILENAME and stated in the header: current-ui describes the layout this extension is written against; constructed-labelled-ui is exactly what it says, built by hand from wordings and shapes justified by evidence in Phase 5 so the cross-layout assertions have a second shape to compare against. It is NOT an observed layout and nothing pretends otherwise; a real capture replaces it the day one arrives. Five assertions: every recorded heading still resolves to the key it resolved to live, which is a regression test for every alias and the whole reason a capture is worth taking; Experience and Education stay separate over real captured wordings, in both directions; every layout produces the same applicant schema, compared key for key at every depth; no layout's distinctive values reach another layout's record; and every fixture on disk still carries no address, no credential and only pseudonyms, so a hand-added one cannot quietly reintroduce an identifier. Two flaws in the tests were found and fixed, both mine rather than the code's: deepKeys descended into arrays, so a layout with an empty Screening section reported a different 'schema' - a fact about the applicant, not the schema - and the leakage check compared pseudonyms, which every fixture assigns independently starting at A, so it was measuring the pseudonymiser rather than the readers. VERIFIED THE SUITE BITES: removing one heading alias from the core (work history) makes it fail, restored and re-run green. Files: tests/applicant-ui-fixtures.test.js (new), tests/fixtures/applicant-ui/current-ui.json (new), tests/fixtures/applicant-ui/constructed-labelled-ui.json (new), docs/CHECKS.md. No production code changed in this phase.
